column3: Lesson one. Lonely is not the same as alone.
Naruto was never physically alone. He was surrounded. What he didn't have was anyone who really saw him.
Psychologists draw the same line. Loneliness isn't simply being alone. It's feeling isolated. The gap between the connection you want, and the connection you have.
That's why you can feel lonely in a crowd. In a classroom. Even in a relationship.
In a famous review, two psychologists argued that people need frequent interactions that aren't negative, inside a bond that lasts. Not just people nearby. People who stay.
So here's the truth underneath it. Being noticed is not the same as being known.
